summary.headline: CONCOR posted record FY26 throughput of 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), but PAT fell 4.5% and Q4 domestic EBIT margin collapsed to 0.2%.
summary.overview: FY26 handling hit a record 5.58 million TEUs (+9.6%), with EXIM at 8% and domestic at 14.6% growth, and rail freight margin rose to 27.16% from 25.65%. PAT declined 4.5% on weaker domestic traffic (gunny bags and Morbi tiles hit by West Asia-related supply disruptions) and tank container shortages. Q4 domestic segment EBIT margin fell to 0.2%, driven by higher empty running and a sharp rise in other expenses. Management guided FY27 handling growth of 9.5% (EXIM 8%, domestic 15%), kept EBITDA margin at 24-25%, and cited the DFC connection to JNPT from 1 June 2026 as a major driver.

segments.name: EXIM
segments.commentary: FY26 EXIM handling 4.21 million TEUs (record), growth 8%; market share fell to 53.9% from 55.2%. Lead distance dropped about 3 km, so revenue grew only about 2.5% against originating volume growth of about 4.5-5%.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q4 segment EBIT margin 0.2%, with revenue down about 4% YoY. Gunny bag (jute) and Morbi tile traffic collapsed, forcing empty container repositioning; Q4 domestic empty running rose 11.3% to INR76.76 crore. Market share fell to 55.9% from 57.6%.

segments.name: Rail and port share
segments.commentary: FY26 rail coefficient: JNPT 15.12% (CONCOR share 60%), Mundra 24.6% (share 35.4%), Pipavav 57.5% (share 48.3%). Overall market share 54.5% vs 55.9% last year.

segments.name: Bulk cement in tank containers
segments.commentary: Fleet of 500 tank containers, adding 200 per month; board approved 2,000 more plus 1,000 earlier. Management targets at least 1 million tonnes of bulk cement in FY27 against domestic loading of 14-15 million tonnes.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: handling volume growth 9.5% overall, EXIM 8%, domestic 15%; management called this conservative and will review at mid-year.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 24-25% in FY27 and beyond.
JNPT rail coefficient expected to rise from 15.12% to about 19% in FY27 (possibly 20-21%) and to 30-35% in about three years.
Capex budget FY27 of INR945 crore approved; may be raised at mid-year review, consistent with ~INR1,000 crore per year.
No long-term (multi-year) volume guidance given; prior reference to 10 million TEUs by FY29-30 not reaffirmed.
Bharat Container Shipping Line (CONCOR 30% stake): investment size not disclosed, pending Cabinet approval.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 43 high-speed rakes in FY26, taking the total to 423; double stack rakes rose to 6,396 from 6,302.
Procured 4,729 containers in FY26, taking own fleet to 57,746 containers.
Empty running of rakes reduced 10.5% overall in FY26 (EXIM -27%, domestic -4%).
DFC connection to JNPT expected to be commissioned on 1 June 2026, with double stack trains from NCR to JNPT.
New double-stack terminals planned at Salawas (near Jodhpur) and Chharodi (near Ahmedabad, on DFC); new terminals commissioned at Mandalgarh, Kadakola (Mysuru), Jajpur and Paradip.
Fleet includes 230 LNG trucks; 5 electric RSTs and 2 electric vehicles on trial.
demand_pricing: Management said EXIM volumes were hit in March and April 2026 by West Asia conflict, with recovery from May; no quantified June-quarter numbers given.
Q4 domestic weakness linked to jute supply disruption (gunny bags) and gas supply shortage closing Morbi tile factories; both were below 50% of normal at the time of the call, with recovery expected.
Double stacking lowers realisation per TEU; lead distance decline cut revenue growth relative to volume growth.
Tariff cuts planned on upper-deck double stack containers (haulage at 50%) to match road pricing; management said Indian Railways has no plan to raise haulage charges.
PSA agreement at JNPT covers domestic plus EXIM and cabotage containers on DFC trains; other JNPT terminals are seeking similar agreements.
Reefer exports grew 17%; DPD volumes grew 38% after liberalised policy.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the JNPT DFC opportunity and rail share outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: JNPT rail coefficient was 15.12% in FY26; management expects about 19% in FY27 and 30-35% in about three years, with tariffs cut on light cargo to match road.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 domestic EBIT margin drop to 0.2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to gunny bag and tile traffic loss forcing empty repositioning from East India. Q4 domestic empty running rose 11.3% to INR76.76 crore; FY domestic empty running fell 3.8% to INR280.35 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said rise reflects higher maintenance, AMC payments and DR site costs, plus CSR; described as recurring. FY26 other expenses INR358 crore; Q4 about INR120 crore versus a typical INR70-80 crore per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth (about 2.5%) far below volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said originating grew about 4.5-5% but lead distance fell about 3 km in EXIM and 12 km in domestic, and double stacking lowers realisation, so revenue lags volume.

qa_highlights.question: What are the investment and capital requirements for Bharat Container Shipping Line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose the investment size, which is pending Cabinet; CONCOR holds 30% and SCI also holds 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the market share and rail coefficient figures?
qa_highlights.answer: EXIM share 53.9% (from 55.2%), domestic 55.9% (from 57.6%), overall 54.5% (from 55.9%); Mundra rail coefficient 24.6% with 35.4% share, Pipavav 57.5% with 48.3% share.

risks_watch: Domestic recovery depends on jute supply resuming and Morbi tile factories restarting; Q4 volumes were still below 50% of normal.
West Asia conflict disruption to EXIM (Middle East exports), with April weak and May recovering; June-quarter impact not quantified.
Rising other expenses (Q4 about INR120 crore vs INR70-80 crore run-rate) and empty running costs threaten EBITDA margin of 24-25%.
Bharat Container Shipping Line investment size undisclosed; capital commitment to be watched once Cabinet approves.
Mid-year guidance review; capex may exceed INR945 crore budget.
Verify DFC commissioning on 1 June 2026 and rollout of JNPT double-stack services and PSA arrangement volumes.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 growth and the DFC/tank container opportunity, but cautious and evasive on specifics: guidance kept conservative, and management declined to share Q4 operating detail, June-quarter empty running, BCSL investment size and PSA terms, citing confidentiality.
key_quotes: We will maintain the EBITDA level between 24% to 25% as we have been doing till now.
Right now, they are below that, but there are indications that very quickly, they will be increasing.
So in the coming years also, we will maintain EBITDA between 24% to 25%. We are quite clear on that.
Yesterday, I'm glad to inform you, Board of Directors further approved the procurement of 2,000 more tank containers, apart from 1,000 tank containers approved earlier.
